The ranking stability is extremely low (tau=0.049) due to a trend-dominated regime, meaning no single model or static weighting is reliable across windows. I will test DBA (Dynamic Bagging of Aggregated models), which adaptively assigns weights per window to mitigate the instability of static rankings.

I will test a weighted combination using inverse error weights on the top 5 models to see if differentiating model quality improves upon the robust ensemble, addressing the "unstable" ranking feature by prioritizing recent performance.

A robust median over the top 5 models is a good baseline, but to improve on the current leader (weighted pool4), I will test a wider pool (pool_full) combined with simple mean to leverage the high predictability and reduce variance from any single model's instability.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w5' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9703. Series context: trend strength 0.9137 and seasonal strength 0.1721; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.049); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.301.
